European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024' (published online 30 January 2025). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. Recorded per the standing owner decision; the article's CC BY-NC-ND licence governs and the content is paraphrased.

claims.claim: **DFSP is a rare fibroblastic skin tumour that invades locally and recurs, but seldom spreads.** Diagnosis is often late, so tumours are large; it grows as irregular, finger-like projections well beyond what is visible.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Incidence is under 1 per 100,000 a year; most patients are 20 to 59.** Survival is excellent (5-year DFSP-specific survival 99.2%).
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It usually starts as a slow, painless, firm plaque of 2 to 5 cm,** most often on the trunk. A sudden growth spurt may mean fibrosarcomatous change.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Think of DFSP when a solitary 'keloid' or hypertrophic scar has no history of injury or surgery;** a small punch biopsy before any big excision avoids mistreatment.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fibrosarcomatous DFSP (10–15% of cases) is more aggressive,** with metastasis risk of 15–20%: stage with CT of chest, abdomen and pelvis plus nodal ultrasound.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm on histology before extensive surgery.** (A)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a deep incisional biopsy, ideally reported by a sarcoma or dermatopathology expert;** keep formalin fixation to 72 h or less so molecular tests remain possible. Diffuse strong CD34 staining is typical.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use CD34 in every suspected case, and re-biopsy if suspicion stays high after a non-diagnostic sample.**
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reports must state whether high mitotic rate or fibrosarcomatous change is present.** (A)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Molecular testing (FISH for COL1A1::PDGFB, present in more than 90%) should be done where possible** (B); about 8% are FISH-negative and may need RNA sequencing or expert review.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contrast MRI can map extent before surgery (C),** especially for tumours over 3 cm, head and neck sites, lesions near bone or joints, or recurrences. Staging scans are not routine except for suspected metastasis, recurrence or FS-DFSP (B).
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Surgery aiming at microscopically clear (R0) margins is first-line for resectable DFSP.** (A)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Micrographically controlled surgery is preferred** (B): Mohs or any technique that examines the whole peripheral and deep margin, usually on paraffin sections. Go down to deep fascia; 1–1.3 cm lateral margins then seem enough.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In comparative studies recurrence was 1.7% after Mohs versus 3.7% after wide excision (not significant),** and micrographic surgery spares more healthy tissue.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Without micrographic surgery, excise with 2–3 cm lateral margins and the underlying fascia;** re-excise invaded margins until clear where feasible. (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reconstruct simply (direct closure, graft or healing by secondary intention), not with flaps,** so recurrence is seen early. (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Resect recurrences with micrographically controlled surgery wherever possible.** (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Imatinib is decided by a multidisciplinary tumour board,** and given before surgery for primary or recurrent tumours that cannot be removed or only with unacceptable harm; operate if the tumour becomes resectable. (B)
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start imatinib at 400 mg/day, increasing to 600–800 mg/day by response;** 400 and 800 mg gave the same response (67.5% vs 67.1%).
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imatinib's European approval covers inoperable primary, locally advanced or recurrent, and metastatic DFSP.** In fibrosarcomatous disease, confirm the fusion in the FS component (FISH or RT-PCR) before starting.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No chemotherapy regimen is established.** Advanced DFSP or FS-DFSP should go to an expert-centre tumour board, with trials where available.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Radiotherapy never replaces adequate surgery and is not given after clear (R0) excision of non-transformed DFSP** (B). It may be added for close margins, recurrence or aggressive subtypes, and as salvage for positive margins.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Curative doses are usually 60 Gy for microscopic and 70 Gy for macroscopic residual disease,** in conventional 2 Gy daily fractions.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FS-DFSP goes to a sarcoma tumour board; standard treatment is complete excision with margins of at least 2 cm.** Micrographic surgery can be considered but is unproven here.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recurrences come late (median 55 months).** After complete excision with low-risk pathology, examine the site every 6 months for 3 years, then every 12 months to year 5 (C). With high-risk features, add MRI 6-monthly for 2 years, then 6–12-monthly to year 5 and at least yearly to year 10. Teach self-examination.
claims.locator: European Association of Dermato-Oncology (EADO), EDF, UEMS and EADV (Saiag P, et al.), European Journal of Cancer 2025;218:115265, 'Diagnosis and treatment of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. European interdisciplinary guideline – update 2024', published online 30 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejca.2025.115265, retrieved 2026-09-23
